sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A rectangular prism is 2 unit cubes long, 3 wide, and 4 high. How many unit cubes fill it?

steps: One layer on the base holds 2 × 3 = 6 cubes.
The prism is 4 layers tall, so it holds 4 copies of that layer: 6 × 4 = 24 cubes.
Counting cubes measures volume, so the answer is 24 cubic units — the base alone, 6 square units, is only one layer.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: Find the volume of a rectangular prism with length 3, width 4, and height 7 units.
An L-shaped solid is decomposed into two non-congruent rectangular prisms sharing a base of 3 by 3 units and having heights 2 and 4 units. What is its combined volume?
A storage box is 6 inches by 4 inches by 3 inches. What is its capacity?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.
